content.value_statement: API teams need accurate specs that match real endpoints. This skill helps create, improve, validate, and document OpenAPI files from code and examples.
actual_capabilities: Draft OpenAPI 3.0 specifications with paths, methods, parameters, and response models.
Add authentication schemes, error responses, examples, tags, and reusable components.
Map API patterns from Express, FastAPI, and Go examples into specification structure.
Suggest CLI workflows for client SDKs, server stubs, documentation, and validation.
Improve specification quality with naming, schema reuse, versioning, and security guidance.
limitations: It depends on accurate source code, route descriptions, or API examples from the user.
It does not verify live API behavior unless the user provides test results or responses.
Generated SDK and validation commands require local tools that the user installs separately.
Authentication, authorization, and data exposure details still need human review.

use_cases.title: Document an Existing REST API
use_cases.description: Convert route files and response examples into a structured OpenAPI draft for review.

use_cases.title: Prepare API Reference Content
use_cases.description: Add descriptions, examples, schemas, and error responses for readable API documentation.

use_cases.title: Generate Client SDK Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan OpenAPI Generator commands for clients, server stubs, and static documentation outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first OpenAPI draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an OpenAPI 3.0 draft for this REST API. Include paths, methods, parameters, responses, and reusable schemas.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to enrich an existing specification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this OpenAPI file and improve descriptions, examples, validation rules, error responses, tags, and security scheme documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Map Routes from Code
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using route handlers or framework annotations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these API route files and produce an OpenAPI spec that reflects endpoints, request bodies, query parameters, and response schemas.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Generation and Validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for delivery workflow planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow to validate this OpenAPI spec, generate a TypeScript client, create documentation, and list required local commands.

output_examples.input: A small user API with list, create, update, delete, login, and refresh routes.
output_examples.output: A structured OpenAPI draft with user schemas, authentication, pagination, validation rules, and standard error responses.

output_examples.input: An incomplete specification that lacks examples, descriptions, and security details.
output_examples.output: A documentation improvement plan plus revised sections for examples, reusable components, scopes, and response descriptions.

output_examples.input: A request to generate a TypeScript client and HTML documentation from an OpenAPI file.
output_examples.output: A command plan covering generator selection, output folders, validation steps, and review checks before publishing.

best_practices: Provide representative request and response examples before asking for a complete specification.
Review generated authentication, authorization, and error responses with the API owner.
Run OpenAPI validation and client generation in a clean branch before publishing changes.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated specs without checking route behavior and sensitive fields.
Do not use fake production URLs, tokens, or credentials in public examples.
Do not generate SDKs from an unvalidated or outdated OpenAPI file.

faq.question: Can this skill create a new OpenAPI file from code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft paths, schemas, parameters, responses, and security sections from route files and examples.

faq.question: Does it support Swagger and OpenAPI?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on OpenAPI 3.0 and uses Swagger tooling terms where common.

faq.question: Can it generate client SDK commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest OpenAPI Generator CLI commands for clients, server stubs, and documentation.

faq.question: Does it run network requests automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill documentation references URLs and tools, but it does not require automatic network access.

faq.question: Should generated specs be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review schemas, authentication, authorization, examples, and sensitive fields before publication.

faq.question: Which users benefit most from this skill?
faq.answer: Backend engineers, platform engineers, and technical writers can use it to document and validate APIs.
